questions.q: Who is responsible for collecting the requirements from different government departments?
questions.a: The Ministry of Finance collects these requirements. A wrong answer suggests the student thinks one single leader or the President does everything, missing the role of the Finance Ministry as the "manager" of government money.

questions.q: Why is the budget process started months before the financial year begins on April 1?
questions.a: It starts early because the government must gather requests from all departments and review them carefully. A wrong answer suggests the student believes it is a quick or random task, ignoring the complexity of managing a country's finances.

questions.q: If the Ministry of Defence asks for more money than the Ministry of Finance has, what happens?
questions.a: The Ministry of Finance reviews and balances all requests against expected income. A wrong answer suggests the student thinks the government can just print or spend unlimited money, ignoring the need for "balancing" a budget.

questions.q: How does the Finance Minister involve the legislature in the budget process?
questions.a: The Minister presents the budget to Parliament for discussion and approval. A wrong answer indicates the student thinks the government can spend money without telling or asking representatives of the people.

questions.q: Is the budget a secret document until it is presented in February?
questions.a: No, it is a public plan that must be presented in the Parliament. A wrong answer suggests the student believes the government acts in secret, rather than being accountable to the citizens through their elected representatives.

questions.q: If you were in charge of a school budget, what is the first thing you would do before spending money?
questions.a: The student should answer that they would ask teachers and students what they need (requests) and check how much money the school has (income). A poor answer ignores the need for planning or consultation, showing a lack of understanding of "budgeting."
